sections.h2: The fastest way to sell in Fort Lauderdale
sections.html:
Selling directly for cash tends to be fastest. The buyer accepts the home as it stands and closes as soon as title is clean. In Fort Lauderdale, settle three questions first. Who owns the property, what is owed against it, and does anyone live in it? Each property carries its own complications: a mortgage payoff, a lease in place, or an estate nobody has opened.

Broward County has 31 municipalities, and Fort Lauderdale is the biggest, ranking among the ten largest cities in Florida. An estimated 188,677 people live here. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $486,700, and owners live in 54.1 percent of homes. At those values, the deed taxes and exemption rules below deserve a careful read.

sections.h2: Homestead after a Fort Lauderdale sale
sections.html:
Legal Florida residents may claim homestead through the Broward County Property Appraiser on a home they make their permanent residence as of January 1. The basic exemption trimmed a Broward owner's bill by between $673 and $1,020 in 2026, with the exact amount tied to the city's millage rate, for homes valued at $75,000 or higher.

Your exemption ends with the sale. The Save Our Homes assessment goes back to just value on the January 1 after ownership changes, so the buyer needs an application of their own.

Whether a buyer gets the exemption in year one comes down to timing. No reason, however good, lets someone file after the September cutoff, so hand your buyer these dates at closing.

sections.h2: What a Fort Lauderdale closing costs
sections.html:
Deeds in Broward are taxed at the usual statewide figure, 70 cents per $100 of consideration, since Miami-Dade is the lone exception. Anyone named on the deed can be held liable, and the Broward clerk takes payment at recording. Section 28.24 governs the per-page recording fees.

Here is who handles each piece:

  • Deed tax and recording: the Broward County Clerk, at recording.
  • Homestead filing: the Broward County Property Appraiser, by March 1 each year.
  • Tax bill: the Broward County Tax Collector, sent in November and delinquent after April 1.

Ask your title company for a closing statement showing every charge before you sign.

sections.h2: When a tenant lives in the house
sections.html:
Having a tenant will not stop a sale, yet the rules for ending a tenancy stay in force. Chapter 83 requires brief written notices for unpaid rent and lease violations, and longer ones that depend on how often rent is paid, with a separate monthly-tenancy rule.

Find out if the buyer will honor the current lease; that sidesteps notices and court. Should you need the tenant to leave, consult a Florida landlord-tenant attorney before serving any paper.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited Fort Lauderdale house
sections.html:
Buyers of an inherited house want to see who is allowed to sign for the estate. Smaller estates may qualify for summary administration, a streamlined court process, while creditors get a fixed window to file claims.

No estate tax applies in Florida for deaths after 2004, and the deed a personal representative signs under a probated will owes no stamp tax. The Broward County Clerk of Courts or a probate attorney can say which procedure suits you.

sections.h2: Homestead paperwork for sellers and new owners
sections.html:
The appraiser asks applicants to bring proof of ownership, usually the recorded deed in the applicant's name. A deed already recorded in Broward's Official Records need not be copied. Where co-owners hold as tenants in common, each owner who lives there must file to claim full coverage.

For married couples and joint tenants with right of survivorship, one owner can secure full coverage, although the office recommends that every eligible owner-occupant file. Trust-held houses follow separate requirements, so phone the office ahead of the sale.

  • Bring identification and proof that the house was your permanent home on January 1.
  • Apply through the office's online portal or in person.
  • Ask about a mobile exemption event if travel is hard.

Acceptance starts the title work: a search for liens and unpaid taxes, and payoff letters from every lender. Then comes the contract, and at closing a deed signed before two witnesses. Lender, stamp tax and recording charges are paid out of your proceeds, with the rest released to you. No buyer's loan means no appraisal and no underwriting step. Judge offers by your net, and decline anyone who wants you to pay before closing.

Putting the house on the market exposes it to the most buyers and may fetch the highest price. It also means showings, repair requests, an appraisal and a financing deal that can collapse. Cash gives up part of that price in return for speed and certainty. Neither answer is right for everyone. A house with a fresh roof and a calm timeline may do well on the market, while one needing work, with a tenant or a lender deadline, often suits a direct buyer better.

Whatever you decide, get offers on paper and add up what each leaves after payoffs, stamps, recording and unpaid taxes.

sections.h2: What to gather before you accept an offer
sections.html:
Early paperwork speeds the title search and takes away a buyer's excuses to reopen the price.

  • The recorded deed, plus trust documents or a probate order if someone other than you is signing.
  • A written payoff from each mortgage lender or lienholder.
  • Permit records for roof, electrical, plumbing and air conditioning work.
  • Any lease and deposit records, if the house is rented.
  • Your latest tax bill and the contact details for any association.

If a document is missing, tell the buyer at the outset. Gaps that are disclosed can often be worked around, while surprises found late tend to end deals.

The title agent goes over the settlement statement with you at the table. Read every figure and ask about anything unfamiliar. After the deed is signed and recorded, keys change hands and your proceeds arrive by wire or check. Afterward, update your mailing address with the Broward appraiser and tax collector so later notices find you, and keep copies of everything you signed.

sections.h2: Checking your record before you list
sections.html: Open the Broward property appraiser's record for your parcel and compare it with your deed. Owner names should match, homestead should appear if you live there, and the mailing address should be current. Fix mismatches before an offer arrives, since a title company will find them anyway. If you did work on the house, confirm the permits are closed. These small checks cost an afternoon and can save a week.

faqs.q: What are Fort Lauderdale homes worth?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $486,700, and owners live in 54.1 percent of homes.

faqs.q: When is the Broward homestead deadline?
faqs.a: Every March 1. The timely window for 2027 closes March 1, 2027, and the last day to late file is September 20, 2027.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax different in Broward?
faqs.a: No, Miami-Dade is the only county with its own rate. Broward applies the statewide 70 cents per $100, which the clerk collects at recording.

faqs.q: How much notice does a month-to-month Broward tenant get?
faqs.a: The minimum depends on the kind of periodic tenancy under chapter 83. Read the statute or ask an attorney before you serve notice.

faqs.q: Can a probate house be sold in Broward?
faqs.a: Usually, after the personal representative has court authority or the estate has completed a short process. Confirm the right path with a probate attorney.
